prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t look up live listings, but I can tell you the best ways to find qualified backflow testing & repair near Liberty, MO and what to ask so you get a safe, legal job done.

Where to look
- Contact the City of Liberty Water Department / Public Works — many cities keep a list of certified backflow testers or require testers to register; they can tell you which testers are already approved to submit test reports.
- Local plumbing companies — most full-service plumbers do backflow testing and repairs.
- Irrigation/sprinkler companies — they commonly test outdoor backflow assemblies.
- Specialized backflow companies — search for “backflow testing” or “backflow prevention service” in Google Maps, Yelp, Angi, or Nextdoor.

What to require/verify
- Certification: ask to see the tester’s backflow tester certification (look for a recognized tester cert such as ASSE 5110 or the state/local equivalent) and the tester’s certification number/expiration date.
- Insurance and business license.
- Proof they will file the test report with the City of Liberty (many cities require the tester to submit results).
- Written estimate for repairs (parts + labor) before work starts.

Typical costs (ballpark)
- Annual test: commonly $35–$125 per device (depends on type/size and region).
- Repairs: highly variable (small part swaps $50–$200; larger repairs or assembly replacement $300–$1,500+).
- Emergency or after-hours work will cost more.

Questions to ask a provider (phone script)
- “Are you certified to test backflow assemblies in Missouri / the City of Liberty? Can you give me your tester certification number?”
- “Do you file the test results with the city, or do I need to submit them?”
- “What is your charge to perform the annual test on a [reduce pressure/dual-check/etc.] assembly?”
- “If a repair is needed, do you give a written estimate first? Do you replace assemblies on-site?”
- “Are you insured and licensed? Can you provide references or online reviews?”

Other tips
- If your property has multiple assemblies (irrigation, fire, domestic), ask about discounts for multiple tests in the same trip.
- Keep a copy of the test certificate for your records; many municipalities need annual testing.
- If you want, give me your zip code or street area and I’ll tell you how to phrase a Google/Yelp search and what search results to expect so you can pick a vendor quickly.

Would you like me to draft a short message you can send to several companies, or a comparison checklist to help decide between quotes?
